purpose: Bridge only the strict-proof gaps that are not already carried by frozen Historie data. Canonical field thinker IDs, names, works and contributions remain authoritative in the existing Historie curriculum/fagkart; this file supplements one missing canonical thinker and scholarly secondary literature for four hand-built fields without mutating frozen V5.8 theory objects, emner or prose.

thinker_supplements.name: Michael Rothberg
thinker_supplements.contribution: Utvikler multidireksjonell hukommelse som ramme for hvordan kollektive minner om Holocaust, kolonialisme og avkolonisering kan sirkulere, overlappe og omforme hverandre i offentlig minnekultur, i stedet for å behandles som et nullsumspill om oppmerksomhet.

works.title: Multidirectional Memory: Remembering the Holocaust in the Age of Decolonization
works.contribution: Boken kobler Holocaust-studier og postkoloniale studier og viser hvordan offentlig erindring kan utvikles gjennom kryssende og gjensidig formende minnebaner.

scholarly_bridge_sources.title: Clues, Myths, and the Historical Method
scholarly_bridge_sources.source_location: 2013 edition, especially ‘Clues: Roots of an Evidential Paradigm’ and the method essays on assigning historical context to fragmentary evidence.
scholarly_bridge_sources.authority: University-press scholarly monograph by a major microhistorian, with explicit method essays on evidential inference and contextual reconstruction.
scholarly_bridge_sources.limitations: The collection supplies methodological and historiographical framing; it does not replace provenance, archival description or claim-specific primary evidence for a Norwegian case.

scholarly_bridge_sources.title: Economy and Society: An Outline of Interpretive Sociology
scholarly_bridge_sources.source_location: Two-volume English edition; use the sections on legitimate domination, bureaucracy, political community, class, status and power as analytical framing for institutions and authority.
scholarly_bridge_sources.authority: Major scholarly edition of Weber’s comparative sociology, published by the University of California Press and foundational for analysis of bureaucracy and legitimate authority.
scholarly_bridge_sources.limitations: Weber’s ideal types are comparative analytical constructions, not a chronology of Norwegian institutions; concrete offices, laws, decisions and administrative practices require independent historical evidence.

scholarly_bridge_sources.title: Coercion, Capital and European States, A.D. 990–1992
scholarly_bridge_sources.source_location: Revised 1993 edition; book-wide comparative argument on coercion, capital, state formation and variation in viable European state forms.
scholarly_bridge_sources.authority: Research monograph in comparative historical sociology from Wiley, explicitly designed to explain variation in European state development rather than a single linear path.
scholarly_bridge_sources.limitations: Its macro-European model cannot by itself establish Norwegian institutional chronology or causation; state-capacity claims must be checked against period-specific Norwegian legal, fiscal and administrative sources.

scholarly_bridge_sources.title: From Viking Stronghold to Christian Kingdom: State Formation in Norway, c. 900–1350
scholarly_bridge_sources.source_location: Book-wide analysis of Norwegian state formation c. 900–1350, including military, socio-economic, ideological, legal and administrative change and comparison with wider European state formation.
scholarly_bridge_sources.authority: Specialist scholarly monograph on medieval Norwegian state formation, published by Museum Tusculanum Press and distributed by the University of Chicago Press.
scholarly_bridge_sources.limitations: The synthetic state-formation argument does not substitute for local archaeological, ecclesiastical or charter evidence; individual churches, rulers and conflicts still require case-specific sources.

scholarly_bridge_sources.title: Medieval Civilization 400–1500
scholarly_bridge_sources.source_location: Part I gives the long chronological narrative; Part II analyzes medieval culture, religion, social structures and the constraints and meanings of time and space in western Europe.
scholarly_bridge_sources.authority: Major scholarly synthesis by a leading medieval historian, published by Blackwell and combining chronological narrative with analytical treatment of medieval institutions and mentalities.
scholarly_bridge_sources.limitations: The synthesis is primarily western European and cannot stand in for Norway-specific evidence on kingship, church organization, law or local religious practice.

scholarly_bridge_sources.title: Utsikt over Norges historie. Tidsrommet 1814–ca. 1860
scholarly_bridge_sources.source_location: Bind 1, tidsrommet 1814–ca. 1860; særlig framstillingen av den nye statsdannelsen, embetsmannsstaten og de politiske institusjonene etter 1814.
scholarly_bridge_sources.authority: Central Norwegian historical synthesis by Jens Arup Seip; Nasjonalbibliotekets 1814-historiography identifies the work as a major modern interpretation of the new state formation.
scholarly_bridge_sources.limitations: The synthesis reflects a specific postwar historiographical interpretation and must be read alongside later research; it cannot alone settle local, social or constitutional details.

scholarly_bridge_sources.title: Demokrati og rettsstat
scholarly_bridge_sources.source_location: Historisk tidsskrift 1979, pp. 1–42; develops the interpretation of the nineteenth-century Norwegian embetsmannsstat as a constitutional state governed through law and constrained power.
scholarly_bridge_sources.authority: Scholarly article in Historisk tidsskrift by Francis Sejersted; later historiography treats the right-state interpretation as a central intervention in the debate on the embetsmannsstat.
scholarly_bridge_sources.limitations: The article is an interpretive intervention in a contested historiographical debate, not neutral evidence for every institution or decision; concrete constitutional and administrative claims require independent sources.
